title: Atalay's Terminal colour theme
description: One theme in the app's own format (ThemeSpec in app/Sources/AtalayTerminal/Themes.swift, 0.16.0 and later). The app makes the rest of its look from these colours. scripts/check.mjs reads its colour rules from this file.

$schema.description: This schema, for editors: "../schemas/theme.schema.json". The app ignores it.

id.description: Unique among every theme the app has. The app saves the chosen theme by it, and the leaderboard shows someone's card by it.

name.description: The name on the theme screen.

bg.description: The terminals' background. The app's surfaces are this colour darkened.

fg.description: The terminals' text. The interface's text shades lie between this and bg.

cursor.description: The terminals' cursor; the text under it takes bg.

selection.description: Selected text's background in the terminals and the code views.

accent.description: Lines, highlights, buttons and the 'working' status. Keep it away from red (ansi 1 and 9): 'needs you' is drawn in red.

ansi.description: The 16 ANSI colours: normal 0-7, bright 8-15. Red (1, 9), green (2, 10), yellow (3), blue (4, 12), magenta (5, 13) and cyan (6) also colour the interface; bright red is 'needs you'.

ui.description: Exact values for the pages' tokens. Colour tokens the app would otherwise make from the colours above ("--accent-soft", "--warn"…) take #rrggbb, their "-rgb" twins take "r, g, b": the native views read them too and draw one they can't read in magenta. Other tokens are free text: "--font" sets the interface's font unless one is picked in Settings, "--theme-id" names the theme to its own CSS.

glow.description: Neon, as SynthWave '84's: the pages' text glows in its own colour with an accent halo, and the terminals, the chats list and the chat windows' headers bloom.
